subject: Pegasus: Reference Safety Gate & Interop Test Plan
messages:
From: Alex Monroe <alex.monroe@pegasus-consulting.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Partnership validation kickoff — reference safety gate

Hi Priya,

Thanks again for the demo last week — our Solutions team is excited about Redwood's latency and routing features. Pegasus Consulting is preparing the technical validation exercise you requested so we can qualify the reference design for our managed offering.

Attached is an initial architecture diagram and a draft integration test plan (pegasus-arch-diagram-v2.pdf, pegasus-integration-test-plan.xlsx). High-level asks from our side:
- Confirm expected token-level latency for Llama-3-70B-v1 under 512-token contexts at 50 concurrent sessions.
- A short checklist for the "safety gate" you use for partner integrations (rate limits, fallback models, provenance headers).
- Any redlines on network topology (we expect to run in AWS us-east-1).

Can we schedule a 45-minute technical sync this week? Our preferred window is Thu 3pm–5pm ET. Sergio (engineering lead) and our QA lead will join.

Attachment(s): pegasus-arch-diagram-v2.pdf (diagram), pegasus-integration-test-plan.xlsx (test cases)

Best,
Alex Monroe
Director, Solutions Engineering
Pegasus Consulting

Alex — thanks for the attachments, they look clear.

We're available Thu 4pm ET (1pm PT). I'll block 45 minutes. Attendees from Redwood: myself (partner lead), Sergio (runtime integrations), Kimberly (security & compliance).

Quick responses to your bullets:
- We'll run a quick benchmark on our Dedicated staging cluster using Llama-3-70B-v1 at 512 tokens to produce a 95th percentile per-token latency estimate; expect preliminary numbers within 48 hours after we get the exact concurrency profile.
- Safety gate checklist (draft): auth & mTLS, request provenance headers, model variant fallback, prefix/KV cache policy, tokenization checks, and anomaly alerting thresholds. We'll share a one-page checklist before the sync.
- Network topology: a minimal allowlist for outbound to our runtime IPs and optionally VPC peering if you prefer private connectivity — we'll include a topology stub.

Please confirm the QPS/concurrency targets in the test plan and whether Pegasus will host sample payloads (recommended). Also parity question: do you expect streaming responses? That affects kernel selection.

See you Thu.

—Priya
Priya Natarajan
Partner Solutions Manager, Redwood Inference

Alex — quick technical notes ahead of the call.

To prepare the runtime validation we need the following from Pegasus (please paste into the test-plan spreadsheet or share a short JSON):
1) Expected concurrency distribution (percentiles for 1, 5, 20, 50, 100 concurrent sessions).
2) Typical prompt/response length distribution (tokens in / tokens out).
3) Whether you will use streaming (server-sent events / chunked responses) or non-streaming.
4) Any request enrichment (metadata headers) that will be present in production.
5) Failure-mode expectations: what are your RPO/RTO targets and what happens on degraded capacity?

On our side, we'll stage a Dedicated node pool that mirrors production quantization flags (int8/awq where applicable) and run:
- Continuous batching with prefix cache enabled
- Model fallback to a trimmed 13B variant for overload scenarios
- KV cache warm-start for common prefixes you provide

If you can provide a sanitized sample corpus (50–200 prompts) and a small workload shape CSV we'll run a 2-hour soak and return latency percentiles, token cost estimates, and a short runbook of tuning knobs that materially impact unit economics.

Attachment: none

Thanks — Sergio
Sergio Alvarez
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime

- Streaming: yes for chat flows; batch for bulk embedding jobs.
